subject: Post-demo synthesis — recommended model trio, benchmarks & ops agenda

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency and context handling very encouraging. A quick recap and the asks we discussed:

- Priority: low single-digit tail latency for short queries (target: 95p < 200ms) and consistent responses for multi-turn workflows.
- Volume: expected steady-state ~12k requests/day, spiking to ~40k/day for seasonal runs; average prompt + response ~350 tokens.
- Data: we'll share a redacted sample corpus (~10k examples) and an initial set of business-critical prompts.

Can you send a short recommended model shortlist (3 options), each with a concise rationale that covers expected cost per 1M tokens, median/95p latency on standard inference config, and any known quality caveats for our QA-heavy use case? Also please include:

- benchmark links and the prompt pack you used for the demo
- proposed pilot scope and duration (what success looks like)
- any operational asks (KV cache sizing, recommended batch sizes, quantization trade-offs) we should prepare for procurement/infra.

Attaching the prompt pack we mentioned (redacted prompts, conversation snippets).

Attachments: vertex_prompt_pack_v1.zip (contains sample prompts + convo snippets)

Appreciate a short note today if possible — aiming to loop in procurement next week.

Best,

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Great demo — next asks and sample data

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the prompt pack. Below is a succinct recommended trio tailored to your latency & QA constraints, plus the operational notes you requested. I attached a short benchmark summary and the prompt pack we used for the demo.

Recommended model trio (prioritized):

1) rw-13b-int8-v2 (balanced)
   - Rationale: Best balance of quality and latency for multi-turn QA. Strong on factuality for retrieval-augmented prompts in our internal evals.
   - Latency (example infra): median ~110ms, 95p ~210ms on dedicated c6g/optimized runtime with continuous batching disabled for small requests.
   - Cost: ~estimated $18 per 1M tokens (hosted profile); efficient with INT8 kernels.
   - Caveats: slightly higher memory footprint than smaller quantized models; performs best with prefix/KV cache enabled for follow-ups.

2) rw-7b-q4f-fast (low-latency)
   - Rationale: Lowest tail latency when tuned; still good quality on short-answer QA and high-throughput endpoints. Good for high-volume query surface.
   - Latency: median ~65ms, 95p ~140ms under small-batch steady-state.
   - Cost: ~estimated $8 per 1M tokens.
   - Caveats: relative drop in long-form or heavy-reasoning QA; recommend prompt engineering and additional retrieval signals for complex queries.

3) open-34b-rtc (high-quality fallback)
   - Rationale: Highest observed factuality and reasoning in our eval set; use as an on-failure or canary for precision-critical flows where cost/latency tradeoffs are acceptable.
   - Latency: median ~340ms, 95p ~620ms (on same infra, depends on sequence length).
   - Cost: ~estimated $55 per 1M tokens.
   - Caveats: higher cost and tail latency; recommend routing only for a small % of traffic (A/B or canary) and using response timeouts.

Operational notes & quick wins:
- KV caching: enable prefix cache for rw-13b-int8-v2; helps multi-turn cost by ~25% for your turn lengths.
- Batching: target small batch sizes (1-4) for latency-sensitive endpoints; use larger batches during off-peak for throughput jobs.
- Quantization: INT8 path on rw-13b-int8-v2 gives good tradeoff; verify for any hallucination-sensitive prompts during pilot.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to rw-7b-q4f-fast for latency SLA breaches, and to open-34b-rtc for precision-critical queries if allowed by budget.

Pilot proposal (2-week):
- Week 0: ingest your redacted sample (we run eval suite), baseline metrics.
- Week 1: deploy rw-7b-q4f-fast for a subset (50%) of non-critical endpoints + rw-13b-int8-v2 for a stratified sample of QA prompts.
- Week 2: measure latency/accuracy, run prompt-regression guardrails, and test open-34b-rtc as a 5% fallback for high-confidence requests.

Success criteria (examples):
- 95p latency < 220ms for rw-13b-int8-v2 on the sample set
- Quality (QA exact/accept %) within 3 points of open-34b-rtc on benchmark set
- Clear cost projection for steady-state below your budget threshold (we'll produce a 90-day projection).

Attachments: benchmark_results_summary.pdf, ops_runbook_draft.md

Next steps
- If this trio looks good, propose we schedule a 30-minute kickoff next Tue or Wed to align infra/procurement and sign the pilot SOW.
- Please confirm whether Vertex can accept occasional routed requests to a higher-latency fallback during the pilot.

I'll spin up a quick shared Drive folder with the workshop artifacts and sample eval dashboards.

Thanks — Nikhil

--

Thanks Nikhil — this is nicely scoped. A few internal ops items before we lock dates: 

- Karthik: can you validate GPU sizing assumptions and whether our dedicated c6g profile matches their region? If not, propose equivalent.
- Ben: please confirm guardrail hooks (prompt-regression alerts + quality regression monitors) we can attach to the pilot; we'll need one test set and a regression threshold to surface to Anna.
- Nikhil: update ops_runbook_draft.md with the recommended KV cache windows (we suggest 48h TTL for their session patterns) and a suggested batch-sizing matrix (latency-sensitive endpoints = 1-4, batchable analytics = 16+).

Also flagging a known edge-case: rw-13b-int8-v2 has been observed to be sensitive to numeric precision in tabular prompts — include a short validation in Week 0 to check for numeric regression.

Marissa
